slides.headline: Less intensity. More frequency.
slides.body: I find myself saying this in nutrition conversations and in stretching sessions. The dial that matters is dose, repeated over time, not the size of any single push.

slides.headline: Strength, conditioning, nutrition. One conversation.
slides.body: The reason I keep returning to dose is that all three disciplines have the same answer when patients ask why a single big effort never sticks.
slides.quoteText: My background's in strength and conditioning and exercise science with a concentration in nutrition

slides.headline: The RDA is a floor, not a ceiling.
slides.body: RDAs were built to keep sailors from getting scurvy. They are the minimum you need to avoid deficiency. Optimum is a different question, and it is the question most patients should be asking.
slides.quoteLabel: WHAT I TELL PATIENTS ABOUT NUTRITION
slides.quoteText: RDAs are based on maritime law — they're the minimum you need to NOT get scurvy, not the optimum to thrive.

slides.headline: Push too hard and the body fights back.
slides.body: Whether the input is a stretch, a workout, or a dietary protocol, hammering at full intensity gets you the same answer. The body braces and the result you wanted gets cancelled out.
slides.quoteLabel: WHAT I TELL PATIENTS ABOUT STRETCHING
slides.quoteText: If we go too intense, too fast, the body's gonna lock up. It gets tight and it won't let go — which defeats the whole purpose.

slides.headline: Lower intensity, longer duration, by the clock.
slides.body: Above a 5 of 10, the body locks up and the position you took stops working. Lower the dial. Hold longer. Treat the stretch like rest, and the range comes.
slides.quoteText: After we start pushing into like 5 plus, the body starts to lock up on us and won't let go — which defeats the perks of the stretch in the first place. That's why I like a lower intensity and a longer stretch, because by absolute time, it's kinda like relaxing.

slides.body: If your nutrition or your mobility plan has you grinding at full intensity and seeing nothing for it, send me a DM and let's adjust the dial.
slides.tagline: Your threshold is higher than they told you.

caption:
Less intensity. More frequency.

I find myself saying this in nutrition conversations and in stretching sessions, almost word for word. Patients arrive convinced that the harder they push, the better the result. Both fields tell the same story when you look at the data: a single big effort gets cancelled out by the body bracing against it.

RDAs were built to keep sailors from scurvy. The minimum you need to avoid deficiency is a long way from the optimum you want to thrive. Most of the supplement plans I review are sitting at the floor.

Stretching is the same problem in a different shape. Above a 5 of 10, the body locks up. Lower the dial, hold longer, return to it daily, and the range comes.

If your plan has you grinding and seeing nothing for it, send me a DM. Let's adjust the dial.
